prompt.context: You are the Vice President of market development for a US mid-sized consumer packaged goods (CPG) company called Personal Care Company (PCC). Your company sells three product lines generating $50M in annual revenues: 1) skin care (with skin protective and sun-blocking properties), 2) tampons (very absorbent features), and 3) baby care bottles (impact resistant). Your company has just been acquired by Prosumer, a global CPG company that makes batteries and shaving products.
prompt.question: How would you recommend increasing PCC's sales from $50M to $100M in 2 years post acquisition?

clarifying_info.q: Are there synergies between Prosumer and PCC?
clarifying_info.a: Yes, there are potential synergies in distribution between Prosumer and PCC related to shaving and skin care products. PCC should look to grow geographically to new markets, focusing on areas greatly exposed to the sun.

clarifying_info.q: Should PCC consider divesting any product lines?
clarifying_info.a: PCC may want to divest another product line (tampon or baby care) if it is not performing as well as sun care, in order to finance the expansion.

clarifying_info.q: What are the international market sizes and growth rates?
clarifying_info.a: US: $5B, 3% growth; Europe: $3B, 6% growth; Asia: $1B, 12% growth; Latin America: $1B, 12% growth.

clarifying_info.q: What is PCC's brand ranking and value proposition in each region?
clarifying_info.a: US: #2 or #3, Functional Care; Europe: #2, Aspirational US lifestyle; Asia: #1, Beauty and fairness; Latin America: #1 or #2, Functional Care.

framework: Assess internal capabilities: review PCC's three product lines, identify which aligns best with growth strategy (sun care as core), consider divesting underperforming lines (tampons or baby care) to fund expansion
Leverage Prosumer synergies: distribution networks, supplier relationships, existing international presence in markets where Prosumer operates
Evaluate international markets: analyze market size, growth rate, brand positioning, and fit with PCC's product functionality across US, Europe, Asia, Latin America
Select priority markets: rank by combination of growth potential, market size, and brand strength
Define market entry strategy: establish suppliers, retail distribution, address competitive reaction, marketing, language/cultural issues, local government regulations
Assess financial feasibility: estimate revenue targets per market, model cost structure including distributor margins, evaluate synergy savings vs. switching costs

questions.prompt: Based on the market data and brand rankings provided, which two international markets would you prioritize first and second for expansion, and why?
questions.guidance: Strong answers identify Asia as the first priority (highest growth at 12%, #1 brand ranking, strong fit with sun-blocking functionality for skin fairness) and Latin America as the second priority (12% growth, #1 or #2 brand ranking, functional care alignment). Candidate should articulate the logic: high growth rate + strong brand position + product-market fit. Europe has lower growth (6%) and a lifestyle positioning that may require more marketing investment. US is already served.

questions.prompt: If the retail price per case is $150, the distributor marks up to the retailer by 50%, and you (the manufacturer) mark up by 100%, what is the cost of each case to manufacture?
questions.guidance: Candidate should work backwards from retail price through the distribution chain. Correct answer is $50 per case.

math.setup: Work backwards from retail price. Retailer pays distributor at retail price divided by (1 + distributor markup). Manufacturer sells to distributor at distributor price divided by (1 + manufacturer markup).

questions.prompt: What are the savings and costs associated with using Prosumer's distributor/supplier network instead of PCC's existing relationships?
questions.guidance: Savings: synergies from using Prosumer's existing supplier and distribution networks already in place; further economies of scale from larger combined volumes. Costs: contract termination costs for ending PCC's current supplier relationship before agreed expiration; sunk costs on existing inventory that the current supplier will no longer support; fees/onboarding costs to the new supplier.

brainstorming.prompt: What considerations are involved in entering the Asian market?

categories.name: Distribution & Supply Chain
ideas: Establishing local suppliers and logistics partners
Leveraging Prosumer's existing Asian distribution network
Retail channel selection (modern trade vs. traditional trade)

categories.name: Competitive Dynamics
ideas: Identifying incumbent competitors and their market share
Anticipating competitive reactions to market entry

categories.name: Marketing & Branding
ideas: Adapting messaging to emphasize beauty and skin fairness
Potential co-branding with Prosumer for credibility

categories.name: Regulatory & Operational
ideas: Local government regulations for cosmetic/personal care products
Cultural nuances in product usage and marketing

categories.name: Financial
ideas: Transfer pricing between Prosumer and PCC entities

recommendation: PCC should leverage Prosumer's global distribution and supplier networks to expand internationally, prioritizing Asia first (high growth, #1 brand, sun-protection fit for skin fairness) and Latin America second (high growth, strong brand, functional care alignment)
PCC should evaluate divesting the tampon or baby care line if capital is needed to fund expansion, retaining sun care as the core growth engine
Marketing strategies must be tailored per region: beauty/fairness positioning in Asia, functional care messaging in Latin America
risks: Switching costs from terminating current supplier contracts may erode early-stage profitability
Competitive retaliation in high-growth markets from established local players
Execution risk in managing simultaneous multi-market entry
next_steps: Conduct detailed market sizing and revenue modeling for Asia and Latin America
Quantify synergy savings vs. supplier switching costs to validate financial case
Develop phased market entry plan beginning with Asia, then Latin America
Assess divestiture options for tampon and/or baby care lines to free up capital
